phases.summary: Created the H-Log phase registry and initial step documents for the blog and automated publishing roadmap.

Steps 0-5 completed: DB content contract, published-only route boundary, Markdown/HTML integrity, safe public rendering, public HTTPS source links, index surface, and non-routed admin workflow contract.
Steps 0-4 completed: OCI runtime topology, Compose service boundary, hardened local Nginx reverse proxy, PostgreSQL backup/restore runbook, and deploy smoke/rollback runbook.

Steps 0-3 completed: publish state transitions, required vs retryable job failure handling, operational audit logging, correction version history, unpublish/retract public removal, and terminal-status republish blocking are tested. Actual OCI server setup remains approval-required before search work.

Steps 0-3 completed. OCI Compose runtime, localhost:8080 Nginx smoke, admin/internal blocking, deploy smoke, logical backup, and isolated pgvector restore rehearsal passed. Production domain/TLS, 80/443 public smoke, and Cloudflare-style admin/internal trust-zone blocking are marked for the later domain purchase/production cutover.

Steps 0-3 completed: hybrid keyword/vector search, /api/search cost guard, fresh post_chunks related similarity, and /blog published-only search UI with cached/loading/empty/rate-limited/error states are tested. No chatbot, SSE, or visitor session memory was added.
Steps 0-3 completed: post-publish verification jobs, crawler outputs, retryable job state handling, and required publish-adapter content-hash verification are tested.

Steps 0-3 completed: source collection/ranking, research pack boundary, apply-to-me context ledger, and claim verification source policy are tested. No external collection, LLM generation, or publishing side effects were added.

Steps 0-3 completed: article writer output schema, persona/mode selection, quality gate publish decision, and bounded daily cron draft-to-publish pipeline are tested. External LLM/API calls and real publish side effects remain adapter-gated.

Steps 0-2 completed: diagram trigger policy, version-bound asset storage, SHA-256 verification, and deterministic public figure insertion are tested without changing canonical Markdown or crawler outputs.

Steps 0-4 completed: PostgreSQL migration and repository, DB-backed public reads, a manual persistent worker, and a deterministic fake-provider Compose dry-run now verify one published success and one private required failure through the real Nginx/public/crawler boundary. No external provider, scheduler, OCI, or production publish activation was added.

Steps 0-10 completed the public-content/privacy decisions, shared shell accessibility baseline, evidence-first Home simplification, career-evidence-aligned Portfolio and Resume surfaces, resilient DB-backed Blog discovery/detail states, complete metadata and crawler coverage, and final DB/HTTP/browser/Lighthouse/doc quality gates. The Go GitHub/Discord automation is separated as a side project, the source PDF remains private, and the Home radar remains unchanged. This completion does not authorize domain, DNS, TLS, OCI, or production timer changes; auto-publish-ops-hardening Step 4 remains approval-required until a real HTTPS public origin and privacy organization/private-repository lists are supplied.
Step 0 completed: aggregate and slug public reads now constrain SQL candidates to published current versions before the privacy scanner and public relation queries run.

Step 0 completed: process-local search history and cache are pruned before evaluation and capped at 100 entries, while embedding usage stays in the durable PostgreSQL ledger and cache-hit published filtering remains intact.

Steps 0-1 completed: database job images use production-only dependencies and the non-root node user, and the confirmed-unused Redis Compose topology was removed. Existing Docker volumes and OCI runtime were not changed.

Steps 0-1 completed: required publish verification shares strict production canonical-origin validation, and Node/Nginx/pgvector/Hermes release bases are digest-pinned with source/rollback records. Lockfile-only production review passed; live registry audit remains separately approval-gated.

Step 0 completed: one fail-fast command runs the five existing PostgreSQL integration suites, and a SHA-pinned GitHub Actions workflow verifies unit, 13 integration tests, typecheck, lint, and build against ephemeral pgvector without production changes.

Step 0 completed: the test-only inline publish/retry branch was removed, generation now has one private-persistence path, and an indexed PostgreSQL existence query rejects persisted slugs before aggregate persistence. Required jobs, retries, and public transition remain exclusively owned by the persistent worker.

Steps 1-6 completed: removed the test-only mutable mirror and confirmed-unused reconciliation, retry executor, persona-learning, performance-signal, and failure-pattern modules while preserving durable duplicate, quality/privacy, and persistent worker boundaries.

Steps 0-2 completed: daily generation verifies claims before private persistence, Hermes writing has no tool capability or model override outside the code-owned gpt-5.6-sol path, and one-shot failures expose only the stage plus redacted gate names and messages without new persistence.

Step 0 completed: the current keyword-only route no longer fabricates embedding accounting. Steps 1-2 will run request guards before PostgreSQL public-store reads and keep submitted search terms aligned with rendered results.

Steps 0-9 will re-check live callers and remove legacy or test-only contracts, a redundant public-slug proxy, unused worker capabilities, and duplicated container defaults while preserving DB-backed public, crawler, retract, claim, rendering, scheduler-egress, and OAuth boundaries.
Steps 0-1 will move legacy project redirects to native Next configuration and share the repeated public-blog date and article-mode presentation rules after search UI alignment.

Steps 0-3 completed. Step 4 artifact 70fd31c is live with server-local credential rotation, production env/input, migrations 001-003, production audit 0, a successful Hermes canary across required/public/crawler/search/usage surfaces, and an audited eight-surface rollback. Timer activation is intentionally deferred until public-site-quality-hardening is complete and a real HTTPS public origin plus privacy organization/private-repository lists are ready for production cutover.

Steps 0-2 established local contracts; all three unwired feedback modules were later removed in code-pruning Steps 4-6 after confirming no live caller or production persistence. Real signal collection and learning contracts remain deferred until HTTPS/privacy/consent runtime requirements exist.
